## Model Planning

### Causal Diagram

![](./causal_diagram.png)

### Model Planning Checklist

Response and key predictor variables:

- Response variable: `received_services_at_catherines`
- Key predictor variable: `income_category` (has `r length(unique(health_survey_df$income_category))` parameters)

Confounders:

- `race_ethnicity`: different racial groups of people might have a larger association with utilizing Catherine's as well as overall household income (has `r length(unique(health_survey_df$race_ethnicity))` parameters).

There are no colliders that we are aware of.

There are no moderators that we are aware of.

Precision covariates:

- `doctor_availability`: If doctor availability is minimal, patients may be more likely to not use Catherines services (has `r length(unique(health_survey_df$doctor_availability))` parameters).
- `wait_time_barrier`: If larger wait times occur, patients may be less likely to utilize Catherines services (has `r length(unique(health_survey_df$wait_time_barrier))` parameters).
- `satisfaction_with_catherines`: If patients are satisfied with the services, they are more likely to utilize them (has `r length(unique(health_survey_df$satisfaction_with_catherines))` parameters).
- `transportation_availability` : If individuals had access to transportation they are more likely to make the trip to utilize Catherines (has `r length(unique(health_survey_df$transportation_availability))` parameters).
- `dental_insurance_coverage`: Patients that are covered by dental insurance may be more likely to use Catherines (has `r length(unique(health_survey_df$dental_insurance_coverage))` parameters).

Mediation chains: 

- `income_category` -> `trust_in_healthcare_system` -> `received_services_at_catherines` : Depends on the income, it will affect people's trust level in healthcare system and this will prevent or encourage them to receive services at Catherines.
- `income_category` -> `health_insurance_barrier` -> `received_services_at_catherines` : Depends on how much income a person receives, it can affect people from having a health insurance or not and depends on how much a health insurance covers it will affect people from receiving services at Catherines.

```{r}
#| include: false

rsc_counts <- table(health_survey_df$received_services_at_catherines)
yes_count <- rsc_counts["Yes"]
no_count <- rsc_counts["No"]
m <- min(yes_count, no_count)
```

The `received_services_at_catherines` variable contains `r yes_count` successes and `r no_count` failures such that $m = \text{min(successes, failures)} = `r m`$. A common rule of thumb suggests that the maximum number of parameters $p$ should be less than or equal to $\frac{m}{15}$, which in this case is $p \leq \frac{`r m`}{15} \approx `r round(m / 15, 0)`$. This means that I may include up to `r round(m / 15, 0)` parameters.

### Model Family and Link Function

Since our response variable is binary, we will use a binary regression model with the logit link function.

## Data Exploration 

```{r}
# Re-ordering
health_survey_df$income_category <- factor(
  health_survey_df$income_category,
  levels = c(
    "Less than $10,000",
    "$10,000 - $14,999",
    "$15,000 - $19,999",
    "$20,000 - $24,999",
    "$25,000 - $34,999",
    "$35,000 - $49,999",
    "$50,000 - $74,999",
    "$75,000 or above",
    "Don't know / Not sure",
    "Refused"
  )
)
```

```{r}
gf_bar(~received_services_at_catherines, fill = ~income_category,
       data = subset(health_survey_df, !is.na(income_category) & 
                     !is.na(received_services_at_catherines)), 
       position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "People Who Are More Affluent Tend Not to Use Catherine's Services.",
    x = "Income", 
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  scale_fill_discrete(name = "Income Category") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Model Fitting

```{r}
health_survey_df$received_services_at_catherines <- factor(
 health_survey_df$received_services_at_catherines, 
 levels = c("No", "Yes")
)  

health_survey_df |>
  pull(received_services_at_catherines) |>
  levels()
```

```{r}
health_survey_df$received_services_at_catherines <- factor(health_survey_df$received_services_at_catherines, 
                                             levels = c("Yes","No"))  
RSC_Model <- glmmTMB(received_services_at_catherines ~ income_category + doctor_availability + wait_time_barrier + satisfaction_with_catherines + transportation_availability + dental_insurance_coverage, data=health_survey_df, family = binomial(link = 'logit'))
```
